title: Peel a hard-boiled egg intact
instruction: Gently crack the hard-boiled egg, peel away its entire shell, and leave the intact egg on the blue plate.
context: Hard-boiled eggs are peeled for serving or use in recipes. The fingertips must free the brittle shell while the second hand supports the soft white. The operation combines a light crack with controlled peeling of the pieces.
setup: On the bimanual YAM bench, a 244 × 225 × 12 mm hardwood board is centered at (300, −50) mm. One cooled large hard-boiled chicken egg (58 × 43 mm, about 60 g) rests intact on its side at (282, −48) with the blunt end toward negative Y. An empty 154 mm blue ceramic plate sits at (320, 148). Coordinates are measured forward and left from the midpoint of the YAM bases.
scoring: 0 if the egg is dropped or visibly damaged, or remains uncracked. 0.20 for a crack after the held egg taps the board. 0.50 after freeing a shell patch at least 10 mm across. 0.80 when no shell fragment at least 2 mm across remains on the intact egg. 1.0 when the peeled egg rests on the blue plate, the removed shell is off the plate, and both grippers are 66 mm clear of the egg center for one second. Inspect with a ruler, photo and video.
reset_notes: Start each trial with a fresh cooled, dry and uncracked large hard-boiled egg in the documented layout. Clean the board, plates and food-contact fingertip covers between trials.
fidelity: Full-size ovoid white, three thin curved shell sections and breakable rigid-body membrane joints approximate irregular fracture and adhesion. Contacts and the pull that frees each piece are native. The rigid white's impact range is checked as a damage proxy. Hairline crack graphics appear after a measured held tap. All separated shell remains physical.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 498 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 820 actions.
